# Full Knowledge Topic Questions

Created: 2026-09-13. Status: question bank prepared; chatbot execution and accuracy scoring have NOT been performed.

## Scope and Counts

The confirmed scope is **academics, others, procedures, services, and university**. The `knowledge/location` directory is excluded. The earlier 700+ estimate included location records; it is not the count of non-location answer topics.

- 16 JSON files.
- 466 records with `responses`, including separate records that share an intent or an answer.
- 95 parent topic containers, covered through all their answer-bearing descendants. A container has no independent answer to grade; the coverage appendix maps it to its cases.
- 21 course-slot item rows and 7 college slot groups, tested separately.
- **494 test sections: 4,940 English + 4,940 Cebuano/Bisaya = 9,880 questions.**
- Every test section has exactly 10 English and 10 Cebuano/Bisaya queries.
- Existing non-location files contain a few navigation-related answers. Those records remain represented for complete file coverage; no separate records from the excluded location database were imported.
- Existing graduate, alumni, and later-year topics remain represented because this is a full data audit. Prioritize freshman topics during user acceptance testing.

The questions were composed from answer content and its intended meaning, not copied from the phrase lists. They use different sentence forms, conversational requests, and selected short or mixed-language scenarios. Some ordinary questions can naturally coincide with existing training text. Reusable question structures make this a synthetic regression bank, not a replacement for independently collected student questions.

## How to Use

1. Send one question at a time in a fresh chat unless a test explicitly supplies prior context. Do not paste an entire section as a single question.
2. Record the case ID, actual answer, language, selected topic if visible in logs, and any incorrect buttons or attachments.
3. Compare meaning against the source reference and answer checkpoint. The checkpoint reproduces current English answer content for review; it does not certify that university policy is factually correct or current.
4. Accept an equivalent duplicate record if the response answers the same question without contradictory details. Do not require literal wording or a particular internal ID when equivalent records exist.
5. Mark each result: **correct / partially answered / wrong topic / clarification needed / unsupported answer / wrong language / data conflict**. If the answer already says information is unavailable, a clear referral is an acceptable answer.
6. For Cebuano/Bisaya, expect a Cebuano response or natural mixed language while retaining official names. Do not fail an answer solely for using an English program name.
7. Keep this bank separate from training phrases for the initial run. Adding these questions to the knowledge phrases before testing would reduce the value of the test.

A percentage from these tests measures performance on this bank only. It cannot establish that every possible real-world query is understood.

## Data Issues to Keep Separate From Routing Failures

- `reschedule_entrance_exam` says an assigned exam cannot be rescheduled; `missed_buksu_cat_schedule` says rescheduling may be possible. Flag conflicting advice for review.
- Preferred-course change records differ: one allows asking ATU for approval, another generally prohibits changes after submission.
- Non-board cutoff records include a historical 2020-2021 figure alongside general current-range guidance. Historical questions should retain their year; do not treat an old score as a current guarantee.
- Several identifiers and answers occur in both academics and admissions. Match the requested meaning and check for contradictions.
- COR validation records give different finance-window instructions. Check source consistency rather than silently selecting one as authoritative.
- Institutional email discovery and institutional email support are separate needs. Looking up issued credentials should not become a generic ICT recovery answer.
- University history records disagree on some founding names, conversion dates, and law numbers. Record these as data conflicts requiring owner confirmation.
- Admission processing-time records give different estimates. These estimates should not be promised as guaranteed dates.
- Some honor-grade descriptions and English/Bisaya shifting guidance need owner review for consistency.
- Deadlines, office holders, fees, ranks, slot counts, and schedules are snapshots. A matching old date is not evidence of a current fact.

## Topic Test Cases

Case IDs remain fixed within this snapshot. A source pointer uses zero-based JSON array indexes. Parent names such as `process` are not globally unique, so use the file and pointer together.

> Here is the key difference between board and non-board courses at BukSU:
>
> - **Board Courses:** Degree programs that require graduates to take and pass a national licensure examination (Board Exam) administered by the Professional Regulation Commission (PRC) or government regulatory body (e.g., Nursing, Teacher Education, Accountancy) before they can legally practice their profession.

Answer checkpoint from the existing data:
> An INC (Incomplete) grade means you still have <b>missing requirements</b> for the subject.
>
> You can complete it by submitting the required activities or outputs requested by your instructor.
>
> You must also submit an INC form to process your completion.
>
> Students are usually given up to one year to complete their INC requirements.
>
> You can download the INC form here: https://drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id=1Au7gJutn9daoM7dJB82IBr20pBjJVrl8

### K159 - Campus Gates & Entrances

Source: [others/facilities_and_other_inquiries.json](<../../../rasa/actions/knowledge/others/facilities_and_other_inquiries.json>), pointer `/topics/28`.
Topic: `campus_gates_and_entrances`. Intent: `campus_gates_and_entrances`.

Answer checkpoint from the existing data:
> BukSU Main Campus has 3 designated campus gates (2 Entrances and 1 Exit):
>
> 1. **Main Pedestrian Entrance (Walking Entrance)**: Located along the front perimeter, this entrance is strictly used for students entering BukSU on foot. *Note: Examinees taking the BukSU College Admission Test (BukSU-CAT) must enter through the Exit Gate instead, as it provides the quickest route to the main examination building (College of Business / COB Building).*
>
> 2. **Vehicle Entrance Gate**: Located on the upper side of BukSU, strictly for vehicle entry only. A valid university gate pass is required to enter BukSU with a vehicle.
>
> 3. **Campus Exit Gate**: Serves as the designated common exit for both pedestrians and vehicles.

### K161 - Withdraw Enrollment Policy

Source: [procedures/academic_transactions.json](<../../../rasa/actions/knowledge/procedures/academic_transactions.json>), pointer `/topics/1/subtopics/0`.
Topic: `process`. Intent: `withdraw_enrollment_policy`.

Answer checkpoint from the existing data:
> To withdraw enrollment, you must submit a Withdrawal Form to the Registrar's Office.
>
> Voluntary withdrawal before midterms results in 'DRP' (Dropped) on your transcript.
>
> Withdrawal after midterms results in a failing grade of 5.0.
>
> You must settle all financial obligations before withdrawal is processed.
>
> The deadline for withdrawal is two weeks before the final examination period.

### K170 - Graduating Clearance Requirements

Source: [procedures/academic_transactions.json](<../../../rasa/actions/knowledge/procedures/academic_transactions.json>), pointer `/topics/4/subtopics/1`.
Topic: `requirements`. Intent: `graduating_clearance_requirements`.

Answer checkpoint from the existing data:
> You can request your University Clearance Form through the BukSU online clearance system.
>
> For your clearance, I suggest completing the process online since an online clearance system is available. First, go to this website:
>
> https://clearance.buksu.edu.ph/
>
> Then, choose student, alumni, or employee depending on your current status.
>
> Log in using your institutional BukSU Gmail account.
>
> Then, click 'Add New Request' located on the top right of the screen and fill out all the details.
>
> Make sure that your clearance details are correct. Note that for the course selection, if you do not see your course immediately, just search for it and it will appear.
>
> After that, click 'Create Request' on the bottom right of your screen.
>
> Please check the portal daily because accountability issues especially unpaid books and other obligations will only be visible on this website.
>
> Make sure to comply with all the requirements. You can click the Request ID to see all pending parts of your clearance, and you may ask the Registrar for more information.

> How can I take the BukSU College Admission Test?
>
> Follow these steps to apply for the BukSU College Admission Test:
>
> Step 1: Access http://admissions.buksu.edu.ph. Register using your active Gmail account. Create your password and re-type it for verification.
>
> Step 2: After creating an account, an email containing a confirmation link will be sent to your Gmail. Check your inbox and click the link to activate your account.
>
> Step 3: Fill out all the necessary information and upload the documentary requirements.
>
> Step 4: Select your preferred schedule (venue, date, and time) based on the availability of slots.
>
> Step 5: You will get notifications when your application is accepted. Once accepted, download and print your Test Permit.

### K179 - Test Permit Name Error

Source: [procedures/admission_procedures.json](<../../../rasa/actions/knowledge/procedures/admission_procedures.json>), pointer `/topics/0/subtopics/5`.
Topic: `test_permit_name_error`. Intent: `test_permit_name_error`.

Answer checkpoint from the existing data:
> What should I do if there is an error in my name on the test permit?
>
> If there is an error in the name or personal information on your BukSU CAT test permit, you should:
>
> 1. Log in to your BukSU Admission account at http://admissions.buksu.edu.ph
>
> 2. Go to your application profile and check the personal information you submitted.
>
> 3. If the name on your application form is also incorrect, edit and correct it, then save the changes.
>
> 4. Re-download your test permit after saving the corrections.
>
> 5. If you are unable to edit your information or the error remains, contact or visit the BukSU Admission and Testing Unit (ATU) as soon as possible  -  ideally before your exam schedule.
>
> Note: Bring both your corrected test permit and a valid government-issued ID on the day of the exam to avoid issues at the testing venue.

Answer checkpoint from the existing data:
> As of current BukSU admission guidelines, incoming first-year students may only take the BukSU College Admission Test (CAT) once per admission cycle.
>
> If you did not reach the qualifying score, BukSU offers the **Affirmative Action Program (AAP)** which may allow non-passers to be considered for admission in select non-board programs.
>
> For AAP assessment, visit the **Diversity and Inclusion Unit (DIU)**. Otherwise, applicants may reapply in the next academic year's admission cycle.

> How to confirm the Intent to Enroll in the BukSU admission portal after passing the CAT?
>
> After the CAT results are released and you have passed:
>
> Step 1: Log in to your BukSU Admission account at http://admissions.buksu.edu.ph using your registered Gmail.
>
> Step 2: Look for the 'Intent to Enroll' or 'Confirm Enrollment' button/option in your dashboard. This option usually appears after the official release of results.
>

>
> Step 4: After confirming, take note of or print the acknowledgment for your records.
>
> Note: Failing to confirm your Intent to Enroll within the given deadline may forfeit your slot. For the exact deadline and steps, check the BukSU ATU Facebook page: https://www.facebook.com/BukSUATU

### K182 - CAT Online vs Walk-in Application

Source: [procedures/admission_procedures.json](<../../../rasa/actions/knowledge/procedures/admission_procedures.json>), pointer `/topics/0/subtopics/8`.
Topic: `cat_online_vs_walkin_application`. Intent: `cat_online_vs_walkin_application`.

Answer checkpoint from the existing data:
> Can I apply as a walk-in for the BukSU CAT, or is it strictly online?
>
> Application and slot registration for the BukSU College Admission Test (CAT) is strictly conducted ONLINE through the official admission website: http://admissions.buksu.edu.ph.
>
> Walk-in applications for exam scheduling are not accommodated because testing slots, venues, and test permits are managed through the online system.
>
> However, the actual examination is conducted in-person (face-to-face) at your selected testing venue and schedule. Be sure to register online, secure your test permit, and bring the required documents on exam day.

### K183 - Exam Fees

Source: [procedures/admission_procedures.json](<../../../rasa/actions/knowledge/procedures/admission_procedures.json>), pointer `/topics/0/subtopics/9`.
Topic: `exam_fees`. Intent: `exam_fees`.

Answer checkpoint from the existing data:
> Are there fees for the College Admission Test?
>
> The BukSU College Admission Test **(BukSU-CAT) is FREE for all Grade 12 students and SHS graduates who have not yet enrolled in college.**
>
> However, applicants who have already completed a bachelors degree or at least enrolled college in BukSU need to pay 300 Php for the Admission Test.
>
> They are not qualified to avail of the benefits of the Free Higher Education.
>
>  REMINDERS
> **No onsite applications** will be accepted on the test day. Only those with approved schedules can take the test.
> **You can only take the BukSU-CAT once every school year.**
> **DO NOT CREATE MULTIPLE ACCOUNTS**

### K192 - Admission Application Approval Time

Source: [procedures/admission_procedures.json](<../../../rasa/actions/knowledge/procedures/admission_procedures.json>), pointer `/topics/1/subtopics/3`.

Answer checkpoint from the existing data:
> How long does it take for BukSU admission applications to be approved?
>
> Admission Officers evaluate and verify applications during regular university working hours (Mondays to Fridays, 8:00 AM  -  5:00 PM, excluding weekends and university holidays).
>
> The standard evaluation and approval process typically takes **3 to 5 working days** after submitting your complete online application and documentary requirements.
>
> You will receive an email notification and a status update on your https://admissions.buksu.edu.ph dashboard once your application is approved.
>
> *(Note: Incomplete, blurred, or non-compliant documents may cause delays in approval or application denial)*

### K193 - Admission Application Rejection Reasons

Source: [procedures/admission_procedures.json](<../../../rasa/actions/knowledge/procedures/admission_procedures.json>), pointer `/topics/1/subtopics/4`.
Topic: `application_always_denied`. Intent: `application_always_denied`.

Answer checkpoint from the existing data:
> Why was my BukSU admission application denied or rejected?
>
> The most common reasons for admission application denial include:
>
> 1. **2x2 Profile Picture Specification**: The photo does not have a pure white background, is not wearing a plain white T-shirt, contains accessories (caps, earrings, sunglasses, headbands), or is distorted/blurry.
>
> 2. **Account Details Discrepancy**: Your full name, contact number, or Gmail address does not match your official school records.
>
> 3. **Documentary & Signature Issues**: The Principal's Certification lacks the official signature or school seal of your Principal, or the scan of your Report Card (Form 138) is unreadable.
>
> **How to Fix:** Log in to https://admissions.buksu.edu.ph, edit your application, replace the flagged photo or document, and re-submit. If your application continues to be denied, visit the Admission Office on the CPAG Building ground floor for assistance.

Source: [procedures/admission_procedures.json](<../../../rasa/actions/knowledge/procedures/admission_procedures.json>), pointer `/topics/2/subtopics/0`.
Topic: `freshman_admission_requirements`. Intent: `freshman_admission_requirements`.

Answer checkpoint from the existing data:
> Here are the requirements you need before applying for BukSU Admission Testing:
>
> 1. You need to have your own personal Gmail account to create an account on BukSU Admissions: https://admissions.buksu.edu.ph/
>
> 2. You need a digital copy of your 2x2 photo. Please make sure your photo meets the following **specifications: plain white background, wearing a white T-shirt, no accessories, and the correct 2x2 size.**
>
> For documentary requirements:
>
> **For current Grade 12 students:** A certification from your school principal that you are currently enrolled in Grade 12
>
> **For SHS graduates:** Copy of your Report Card or High School Diploma
>
> **For Transferees:** Transcript of Records or Honorable Dismissal, or a certification from your current school's Registrar
>
> **For Returnees** (stopped studying in BukSU before 2018): Request a certification from the Registrar through this link: https://forms.gle/aKoX7zTJmnTSBNNFA
>
> **For Second Courser:** Transcript of Records. (If it has been more than five years since your last school attendance, you must take the College Admission Test and pay 300 testing fee)
>
> After applying for BukSU Admission, please wait for approval.
>
> Note: Your Gmail should be accessible, as all verification codes will be sent there.

### K204 - Transferee Admission Requirements

Source: [procedures/admission_procedures.json](<../../../rasa/actions/knowledge/procedures/admission_procedures.json>), pointer `/topics/2/subtopics/1`.
Topic: `transferee_admission_requirements`. Intent: `transferee_admission_requirements`.

Answer checkpoint from the existing data:
> Yes BukSU accepts transferees depending on the availability of slots in the chosen program. You must first take and pass the BukSU Admission before you can enroll as a transferee.
>
> Once you pass the admission, proceed to the BukSU main campus and go to the college department where you plan to enroll.
>
> Transferees must submit an Honorable Dismissal and an Informative Copy of their Transcript of Records for evaluation, meet the required GWA, and pass any admission interview or exam.
>
> Since each department may have its own specific rules for transferees, it is best to ask a faculty or staff member directly in the office for proper guidance.

### K226 - SIAS Forgot Password

Source: [procedures/admission_procedures.json](<../../../rasa/actions/knowledge/procedures/admission_procedures.json>), pointer `/topics/4/subtopics/7`.
Topic: `sias_forgot_password`. Intent: `sias_forgot_password`.

Answer checkpoint from the existing data:
> To reset your SIAS password, open <b>https://sias.buksu.edu.ph/sias/</b>.
>
> Click <b>Student</b> if you are a student. Choose the correct role if you are an instructor or another user type.
>
> Type your Student ID first, then click the <b>Forgot Password</b> button located below the Login button.
>
> Type your institutional email or student email, then click <b>Send code</b>. Open your email account and wait for the code.
>
> Type the code, enter your new password, retype the password to confirm, then click <b>OK</b>. After that, you can log in to your SIAS account.

### K230 - Affirmative Action

Source: [procedures/admission_procedures.json](<../../../rasa/actions/knowledge/procedures/admission_procedures.json>), pointer `/topics/5/subtopics/0`.
Topic: `affirmative_action`. Intent: `affirmative_action`.

Answer checkpoint from the existing data:
> If you failed your BukSU cat examination you still have a choice, you can apply for Affirmative Action Program (AAP) but please note that you cannot choose the courses you want to enroll in, they will be the one choosing your program depends on your capability.
>
> here how you can apply the AAP
>
> 1. Monitor Your Results: Check your Report of Rating (ROR) via the BukSU Admissions Portal. Even if you are not on the list of <b>Qualifiers</b>, keep your account credentials. https://admissions.buksu.edu.ph/
>
> 2 Go to the Diversity and Inclusion Unit located at the BukSU Main Campus in Malaybalay City. This unit manages the AAP selection.
>
> 3. Submit Supporting Documents: You will need to provide proof of your eligibility, such as:<div><span style="color: rgb(15, 23, 41);"><b>For IPs</b>: Certificate of Tribal Membership or NCIP Certificate.</span></div><div><span style="color: rgb(15, 23, 41);"><b>For PWDs:</b> Valid PWD ID.</span></div><div><span style="color: rgb(15, 23, 41);"><b>For Low-Income: </b>Certificate of Indigency from your Barangay or ITR of parents.</span></div><div><span style="color: rgb(15, 23, 41);"><b>Academic Records:</b> Your Senior High School Report Card (Form 138).</span></div>
>
> 4. Interview/Evaluation: The Diversity and Inclusion Unit may conduct an interview to assess your <b>academic potential</b> and commitment to finishing the degree.
>
> 5. Placement: If approved, you may be offered a slot in a program that still has available capacity (note that highly competitive board courses like Nursing or Accountancy often have stricter cut-offs that AAP cannot always bypass).

### K239 - Returning Student Readmission

Source: [procedures/admission_procedures.json](<../../../rasa/actions/knowledge/procedures/admission_procedures.json>), pointer `/topics/13`.
Topic: `returning_student_readmission_process`. Intent: `returning_student_readmission_process`.

Answer checkpoint from the existing data:
> Here is the readmission and enrollment process for Returning Students (Balik-Aral):
>
> - **Important Policies**:
> - Students who were under the **old curriculum** must re-enter the course as a first-year student.
> - If it has been **more than 5 years** since your last semester of attendance, university policy dictates that you must retake the BukSU College Admission Test (BukSU-CAT) and pay a PHP 300 testing fee to be reintegrated.
>
> - **Step-by-Step Readmission Procedure**:
> 1. Register online at: https://admissions.buksu.edu.ph
> 2. Activate your account via email (click the activation link).
> 3. Update your Account Information.
> 4. Click 'Proceed to Account Migration' and use your previous student number to migrate your account.
> 5. Apply for Enrollment.
> 6. Steps 1 - 5: Complete all required information.
> 7. Step 6: Verify, sign, and confirm your Enrollment Application.
> 8. Submit and wait for your Evaluator to process your Enrollment Application.
> 9. Retrieve and review your Certificate of Registration (COR).
>
> For the complete official guide, visit: https://admissions.buksu.edu.ph/posts/12/

English:

### K240 - Enrollment General Process

Source: [procedures/enrollment_procedures.json](<../../../rasa/actions/knowledge/procedures/enrollment_procedures.json>), pointer `/topics/0/subtopics/0`.
Topic: `enrollment_general_process`. Intent: `enrollment_general_process`.

Answer checkpoint from the existing data:
> Here is the step-by-step enrollment process for **Undergraduate Programs, Law & Graduate Programs, and College of Medicine**. Please note that all the data we provided are **General**. If you are finding a specific process, you should directly ask any of the faculty staff in your department.
>
> Step 1. You may look on the picture provided below for the requirements needed.
>
> Step 2: Login to https://admissions.buksu.edu.ph 
> - Click on **Admission**
> - Click **Show Exam Result** then proceed to enrollment
> - Click **Apply Enrollment** 
> - **Campus Selection**: Select **Main Campus** 
> - **Course Selection**: Select your **Preferred Course** 
> - **Documentary Requirements**: Scan and upload the documentary requirements as specified in Step 1 
> *(NOTE: All documents uploaded as part of the admission process must be duly marked with a "RECEIVED" stamp by the University Registrar's Office)* 
> - **Learning Modality Preference**: Select your **Preferred Learning Modality** 
> - **Academic Information**: Fill in the necessary information
>
> Step 3: Approval of Enrollment Application
>
> Wait for the evaluator's approval of your application. Once your application is approved, download your Certificate of Registration (COR) through https://admissions.buksu.edu.ph
>
> *(Click 'Report Incorrect COR' if you find any errors)*
>
> Step 4: Validation of Enrollment, you may look on the image provided below.

### K241 - Enrollment - Where to Start

Source: [procedures/enrollment_procedures.json](<../../../rasa/actions/knowledge/procedures/enrollment_procedures.json>), pointer `/topics/0/subtopics/1`.
Topic: `enrollment_where_to_start`. Intent: `enrollment_where_to_start`.

Answer checkpoint from the existing data:
> Welcome! Don't worry  -  let me walk you through the full enrollment journey step by step. Here's what you need to do as an **incoming freshman or transferee** at BukSU:
> 
> **Step 1: Pass the BukSU College Admission Test (BukSU-CAT)**
> Before you can enroll, you must first take and pass the BukSU entrance examination. You can apply for the CAT at https://admissions.buksu.edu.ph.
> 
> **Step 2: Check your Exam Result**
> Once the results are released, log in to the same portal to check your score and admission status.
> 
> **Step 3: Apply for Enrollment Online**
> If you passed, proceed to your online enrollment application:
> - Go to https://admissions.buksu.edu.ph
> - Click **Admission  Show Exam Result**, then click **Apply Enrollment**
> - Select your **Campus**, **Preferred Course**, and upload your **Documentary Requirements**
> 
> **Step 4: Wait for Approval**
> Wait for the evaluator's approval. Once approved, download your **Certificate of Registration (COR)**.
> 
> **Step 5: Validate your COR**
> Go to **Window 7** at the Finance Building to get your COR validated.
> 
> **Step 6: Pay your Tuition**
> Proceed to the **Cashier's Office (Window 3)** at the Finance Building to settle your fees.
> 
> You can also ask me about any specific step above  -  I'm here to help!

### K242 - Mixed / Onsite Enrollment Process

Source: [procedures/enrollment_procedures.json](<../../../rasa/actions/knowledge/procedures/enrollment_procedures.json>), pointer `/topics/0/subtopics/2`.
Topic: `mixed_enrollment_process`. Intent: `mixed_enrollment_process`.

Answer checkpoint from the existing data:
> For Face-to-Face or mixed enrollment, the initial process is similar to online enrollment - fill up the requirements on the BukSU Admissions portal.
>
> After completing your online application, proceed to your department to process your pending enrollment. Dedicated faculty staff handle department enrollment. Follow any queue system or line numbers provided.
>
> For 2nd year students and above, you will process directly with your department evaluators.
>
> For Incoming Freshmen and Transferees:
> 1. Attend the Pre-enrolment Orientation.
> 2. Proceed to your college of choice for personal interview and present documents in a long brown envelope for evaluation.
> 3. Proceed to the I.T. Laboratory for Information System Registration and document submission.

### K246 - Freshman Enrollment Requirements

Source: [procedures/enrollment_procedures.json](<../../../rasa/actions/knowledge/procedures/enrollment_procedures.json>), pointer `/topics/0/subtopics/6`.
Topic: `freshman_enrollment_process`. Intent: `freshman_enrollment_process`.

Answer checkpoint from the existing data:
> Make sure you pass the entrance examination, and prepare these requirements. It should be 2 envelopes: Envelope 1 is the Registrar's Copy, and Envelope 2 is the Student's Copy.
> 
> 1. Program Acceptance Slip
> 2. Report Card
> 3. Good Moral
> 4. Honorable Dismissal (for Transferees only)
> 5. Transcript of Records (for Transferees only)
> 6. Subject Equivalency Form (for Transferees only)
> 7. Photocopy of PSA Birth Certificate
> 8. Photocopy of Marriage Contract (if Married)
> 9. BukSU-CAT Report of Rating
> 10. Photocopy of Medical Certificate
>
> Requirements to be submitted to the department/program:
> 
> 1. Medical Certificate (The Medical Certificate must be issued by a government Physician and must state that the student is physically fit for "OFF-CAMPUS AND IN-CAMPUS ACTIVITY"). (Original Copy)
> 2. NOTARIZED GENERAL PARENTAL/GUARDIAN CONSENT FORM (Original Copy)
> 
> Download the form here: https://buksu.edu.ph/downloadable-forms/
>
>  **PROGRAM-SPECIFIC ADVISORY (e.g., BSIT, Nursing, BSBA, Education, etc.):**
> While the documents above are the general institutional enrollment requirements for BukSU, specific programs (such as BSIT, Nursing, Accountancy, Education, etc.) may have additional department-level qualifying cutoffs, interview schedules, skill assessments, or program-specific medical guidelines.
> 
>  For program-specific announcements, qualifying updates, and interview dates for your chosen course, please visit your official College / Department Facebook Page or check https://admissions.buksu.edu.ph/courses

> 
>  **BukSU Admissions Portal**: https://admissions.buksu.edu.ph
> 
> **Through this portal, applicants and incoming students can:**
> - Apply for the BukSU College Admission Test (BukSU-CAT)
> - Check entrance examination results and admission status
> - Submit online enrollment applications and upload required documents
> - Download the approved Certificate of Registration (COR)
> 
> **For officially enrolled / continuing students:**
>  **SIAS Portal** (http://sias.buksu.edu.ph) is used to access study loads, enrolled subjects, and grades.

### K248 - Online Enrollment Application Steps

Source: [procedures/enrollment_procedures.json](<../../../rasa/actions/knowledge/procedures/enrollment_procedures.json>), pointer `/topics/0/subtopics/8`.
Topic: `online_enrollment_steps`. Intent: `online_enrollment_steps`.

Answer checkpoint from the existing data:
> Step 2 of the enrollment process is the Online Enrollment Application through https://admissions.buksu.edu.ph.
>
> The Online Enrollment Application will be open on July 1, 2026.
>
> After logging in, click Admission.
>
> Click Show Exam Result, then proceed to Enrollment.
>
> Click Apply Enrollment.
>
> Under Campus Selection, select Main Campus.
>
> Under Course Selection, select your preferred course.
>
> Under Documentary Requirements, scan and upload the documentary requirements specified in Step 1. Documents uploaded during admission must be duly marked with a RECEIVED stamp by the University Registrar's Office.
>
> Under Learning Modality Preference, select your preferred learning modality.
>
> Under Academic Information, fill in the necessary information.
>
> Even if you apply for online enrollment, please wait for the announcement from your specific department because some departments may still require you to go to the faculty office for actual enrollment confirmation.

### K252 - Enrollment Validation and Payment Process

Source: [procedures/enrollment_procedures.json](<../../../rasa/actions/knowledge/procedures/enrollment_procedures.json>), pointer `/topics/0/subtopics/12`.
Topic: `enrollment_validation_payment`. Intent: `enrollment_validation_payment`.

Answer checkpoint from the existing data:
> Step 4 is Validation of Enrollment from July 1 to August 31, 2026.
>
> For on-site payment: print your Certificate of Registration (COR), then proceed to the Accounting Office, Windows 3 to 5, for account verification. This applies to both paying and non-paying students.
>
> For paying students, pay at the Cashier's Office Window 10.
>
> After account verification or payment, proceed to the University Registrar's Office for enrollment validation. This applies to both paying and non-paying students.
>
> For online payment: access your COR through https://admissions.buksu.edu.ph to determine the required down payment for official enrollment.
>
> Go to https://www.lbp-eservices.com/egps/portal/index.jsp, click Pay Now, search and select Merchant Name: Bukidnon State University, then click Continue.
>
> Select the transaction type Tuition and Other School Fees, then click Continue. Fill out the transaction details, choose your preferred payment mode, input the captcha, agree to the Terms and Conditions, and submit the payment details including OTP and ATM PIN if required.
>
> You can view your enrollment status through SIAS Online 10 working days after payment.

### K253 - Law and Graduate Enrollment Requirements

Source: [procedures/enrollment_procedures.json](<../../../rasa/actions/knowledge/procedures/enrollment_procedures.json>), pointer `/topics/0/subtopics/13`.
Topic: `graduate_law_enrollment_requirements`. Intent: `graduate_law_enrollment_requirements`.

Answer checkpoint from the existing data:
> Make sure you pass the entrance examination, and prepare these requirements. It should be 2 envelopes: Envelope 1 is the Registrar's Copy, and Envelope 2 is the Student's Copy.
> 
> 1. Program Acceptance Slip
> 2. Honorable Dismissal (for non-BukSU graduates only)
> 3. Transcript of Records
> 4. Subject Equivalency Form (for Transferees)
> 5. Photocopy of PSA Birth Certificate
> 6. Photocopy of Marriage Contract (if Married)
> 7. BukSU-CAT Report of Rating
> 8. Photocopy of Medical Certificate
> 9. Photocopy of Waiver
>
> Requirements to be submitted to the department/program:
> 
> 1. Medical Certificate (The Medical Certificate must be issued by a government Physician and must state that the student is physically fit for "OFF-CAMPUS AND IN-CAMPUS ACTIVITY"). (Original Copy)
> 2. NOTARIZED WAIVER AND RELEASE FOR GRADUATE AND POST-GRADUATE STUDENTS (Original Copy)
> 
> Download the form here: https://buksu.edu.ph/downloadable-forms/

### K255 - CON Nursing Enrollment Guidance

Source: [procedures/enrollment_procedures.json](<../../../rasa/actions/knowledge/procedures/enrollment_procedures.json>), pointer `/topics/0/subtopics/15`.
Topic: `con_nursing_enrollment_guidance`. Intent: `con_nursing_enrollment_guidance`.

Answer checkpoint from the existing data:
> For incoming First Year Nursing students, especially waitlisted applicants who became eligible to enroll, please go directly to the College of Nursing (CON).
>
> CON can release your acceptance slip and other forms, and they will also give the official instructions on what to do next.
>
> For medical requirements, follow the checklist or forms given by CON. If a medical laboratory examination is needed, you may look for a medical laboratory nearby or any laboratory accepted by the college instruction.
>
> If you do not have an immunization or vaccine record, go to your barangay health center or the health center where you were immunized and request a certificate or record of your immunization.
>
> For the process of submitting requirements, follow the instruction given by CON after you receive your acceptance slip and forms.

Topic: `paying_student_definition`. Intent: `paying_student_definition`.

Answer checkpoint from the existing data:
> A paying student is a student who needs to pay the assessed tuition and/or other school fees for the enrollment period.
>
> This can happen if the student is not eligible for Free Higher Education, voluntarily opts out of the free higher education benefit, or has charges that are assessed separately by the university.
>
> For program-specific assessment, especially if you see payment instructions in your COR, verify directly with the Accounting Office, Registrar, or your college because the chatbot should not assume your final payment status.

### K263 - Paying and Non-Paying Student Difference

Source: [procedures/enrollment_procedures.json](<../../../rasa/actions/knowledge/procedures/enrollment_procedures.json>), pointer `/topics/2/subtopics/3`.
Topic: `paying_and_non_paying_students`. Intent: `paying_and_non_paying_students`.

Answer checkpoint from the existing data:
> Paying students and non-paying students are different based on how their tuition and school fees are assessed during enrollment.
>
> Paying student: a student who needs to pay assessed tuition and/or other school fees. This may happen if the student is not eligible for Free Higher Education, voluntarily opts out, or has assessed charges that are not covered by the benefit.
>
> Non-paying student: a student whose tuition and covered school fees are under the Free Higher Education benefit.
>
> Important: Do not assume that a specific course is automatically paying or non-paying. For final payment status, check the COR and verify with Accounting, Registrar, or your college.

> For transferees, you must first take and pass the BukSU Admission process before you can enroll.
>
> After passing admission, proceed to the college or department where you plan to enroll so your academic records can be evaluated.
>
> Prepare transferee-related documents such as Honorable Dismissal, Transcript of Records or informative copy, Subject Equivalency Form if required, and the other enrollment documentary requirements listed for undergraduate first year/transferee applicants.
>
> Once your documents are evaluated, follow the online enrollment application steps through https://admissions.buksu.edu.ph and wait for your department or evaluator instructions.
>
> For private school transferees, expect possible delays because previously taken subjects may need additional evaluation and may not all be credited.

### K268 - PSA Birth Certificate Requirement

Source: [procedures/enrollment_procedures.json](<../../../rasa/actions/knowledge/procedures/enrollment_procedures.json>), pointer `/topics/4/subtopics/3`.
Topic: `psa_birth_certificate_requirement`. Intent: `psa_birth_certificate_requirement`.

Answer checkpoint from the existing data:
> For official enrollment, BukSU requires the **Original PSA Birth Certificate** along with 2 clear photocopies for the Registrar's permanent student records.
>
> If your PSA copy is currently delayed, you may temporarily present a Certified True Copy from the Local Civil Registrar (LCR), provided you sign a promissory note with the University Registrar to submit the original PSA copy within the semester.
>
> Make sure your name, birth date, and parents' names on the PSA match your school records (Form 138 / SHS diploma) to prevent credential discrepancies.

### K269 - Incoming Freshmen SIAS Claim

Source: [procedures/enrollment_procedures.json](<../../../rasa/actions/knowledge/procedures/enrollment_procedures.json>), pointer `/topics/4/subtopics/4`.
Topic: `sias_first_year_claim`. Intent: `sias_first_year_claim`.

Answer checkpoint from the existing data:
> How do incoming first-year students claim their SIAS account and default password?
>
> For incoming first-year students, your SIAS (Student Information Accounting System) account is automatically generated after your on-site enrollment is validated and your Certificate of Registration (COR) is approved by the Registrar.
>
> Your **Student ID Number** (found at the top of your COR) serves as your SIAS Username.
>
> To log in: 1. Access https://sias.buksu.edu.ph/sias/. 2. If you don't know your default password, click **'Find SIAS Account'** or **'Forgot Password'** and enter your registered email address. 3. If you still cannot access it, visit the ICT Service Unit (ICTU) or the Registrar's Office for account activation.

### K270 - Late Document Submission Policy

Source: [procedures/enrollment_procedures.json](<../../../rasa/actions/knowledge/procedures/enrollment_procedures.json>), pointer `/topics/4/subtopics/5`.
Topic: `late_enrollment_document_submission`. Intent: `late_enrollment_document_submission`.

Answer checkpoint from the existing data:
> What happens if I submit my enrollment documents late?
>
> Late submission of required enrollment documents may cause delays in validating your Certificate of Registration (COR) and finalizing your official subject enlistment in the SIAS system.
>
> If your documents are not submitted within the prescribed enrollment extension period, your temporary reservation/slot may be placed on hold or forfeited in favor of waitlisted applicants.
>
> If you are experiencing document delays (e.g. late release of Form 138 from your high school or PSA certificate), coordinate immediately with the Office of the University Registrar and file a promissory request before the deadline.

### K280 - Campus Entry Without Student ID

Source: [procedures/student_service_procedures.json](<../../../rasa/actions/knowledge/procedures/student_service_procedures.json>), pointer `/topics/0/subtopics/4`.
Topic: `campus_entry_without_student_id`. Intent: `campus_entry_without_student_id`.

Answer checkpoint from the existing data:
> Yes, students without a physical ID are usually allowed during the first month of the school year, especially first-year students who do not have their ID yet.
>
> You can present your validated COR to the entrance guard so they can verify that you are an officially enrolled first-year student.
>
> <b>Make sure it is a validated COR</b>, and explain clearly why you do not have your student ID yet.
>
> If you lost your student ID, ask the guard about the entry process and explain why your ID is missing. Make sure to bring your validated COR.
>
> If you only forgot your student ID, it is better to go back and bring it. If that is not possible, ask the guard if there is another way to enter temporarily.
>
> Always bring your student ID when entering campus. If you do not have one yet, process your student ID at the University Press.

> Total duration is 28 minutes, with zero cost.

### K299 - Institutional Email Account Help

Source: [procedures/student_service_procedures.json](<../../../rasa/actions/knowledge/procedures/student_service_procedures.json>), pointer `/topics/6/subtopics/3`.
Topic: `institutional_email_account`. Intent: `institutional_email_account`.

Answer checkpoint from the existing data:
> Your official BukSU student email address is your institutional email account. It is different from your BukSU Admission account.
>
> For your official BukSU institutional email or student email login, go to the ICT office on the 3rd floor of the Finance Building and ask for assistance with your institutional email account.
>
> Bring your validated COR or student ID if available, because ICT may need to verify that you are an officially enrolled student.
>
> Students may also ask ICT for help if they forgot their institutional email, cannot log in, or need account recovery.

Answer checkpoint from the existing data:
> Turn on your Wi-Fi.
>
> Find and select **Student_wifi** (please do not connect to 'Student_Wifi2.0' and other versions since there is only one official student Wi-Fi).
>
> Wait until you are fully connected, and there will be a sign-in option on the Student_wifi. Press that and enter your credentials (Student ID and password).
>
> You are successfully connected. Please note that under other circumstances, the student Wi-Fi in that specific area might be full (connections are full), or the student Wi-Fi is far from the area where you standby, which is why it won't connect easily.

### K325 - Request Tooth Extraction

Source: [services/clinic_services.json](<../../../rasa/actions/knowledge/services/clinic_services.json>), pointer `/topics/1/subtopics/6`.
Topic: `request_tooth_extraction`. Intent: `request_tooth_extraction`.

Answer checkpoint from the existing data:
> Ask the clinic for the cost first since I don't have data for the tooth extraction cost.
>
> Here is the process of Request for Tooth Extraction.
>
> Submit photocopies of validated school ID and validated study load.
>
> Submit complied waiver from parents or guardian. Note: If below 18 years old, the patient needs parent or guardian permission. If 18 years old and above, no need to present waiver.
>
> Client proceeds to the vital signs taking area.
>
> Client shares his or her case history to the Administrative Aide III.
>
> Client proceeds to the dental chair for tooth extraction procedure.
>
> Receive medicines and fill out the medicine ledger and monthly dental report form.
>
> Total duration is 1 hour and 8 minutes to 1 hour and 38 minutes.

### K344 - Library Entry Without Physical ID

Source: [services/library_services.json](<../../../rasa/actions/knowledge/services/library_services.json>), pointer `/topics/1/subtopics/1`.
Topic: `library_entry_without_id`. Intent: `library_entry_without_id`.

Answer checkpoint from the existing data:
> Can I enter the BukSU University Library if I don't have a physical student ID card yet?
>
> Yes, incoming first-year students and new students who have not yet received their physical Student ID / Library Card are still permitted to enter the BukSU University Library.
>
> Requirements for entry without physical ID: 1. Present your validated **Certificate of Registration (COR)** as proof of enrollment for the current semester. 2. Present any valid alternative photo ID (such as your SHS ID or valid government ID). 3. Sign the visitor/temporary entry logbook at the library entrance.
>
> Once your official Student ID or barcoded Library Card is issued, you will use it for standard tap/scan entry and borrowing.

### K362 - Civilian Attire & Dress Code Policy

Source: [services/oss_student_services.json](<../../../rasa/actions/knowledge/services/oss_student_services.json>), pointer `/topics/2/subtopics/0`.
Topic: `wear_civilian_attire`. Intent: `wear_civilian_attire`.

Answer checkpoint from the existing data:
> **University Memorandum No. 01, s. 2026  -  Prescribed University Uniform Policy:**
>
> Please be informed that all students are required to wear the complete prescribed university uniform every **Monday**, **Tuesday**, **Thursday**, and **Friday**, effective on their respective dates:
> 
> - **2ND YEAR - 4TH YEAR STUDENTS:** Effective **September 7, 2026**
> - **1ST YEAR STUDENTS:** Effective **September 14, 2026**
>
> Students are expected to **strictly observe the prescribed university uniform policy** on the indicated days.
>
> Civilian attire (such as decent T-shirts and long pants/jeans) is permitted on **Wednesdays (Wash Days)**, Saturdays, Sundays, and during official university wash-day announcements or enrollment periods.
>
> Note: Sandos/sleeveless shirts, short shorts, ripped/revealing clothing, and rubber slippers are strictly prohibited on campus during class days and office hours.

### K363 - Haircut and Hair Color Policy

Source: [services/oss_student_services.json](<../../../rasa/actions/knowledge/services/oss_student_services.json>), pointer `/topics/2/subtopics/1`.
Topic: `haircut_and_hair_color_policy`. Intent: `haircut_and_hair_color_policy`.

Answer checkpoint from the existing data:
> What is BukSU's policy on haircut and colored hair?
>
> According to the BukSU Student Handbook guidelines on grooming and campus decorum:
>
> 1. Students are expected to maintain neat, clean, and respectable hairstyles while on campus.
>
> 2. For male students in general undergraduate programs, modest and well-groomed haircuts are expected. Extreme or unkempt styles are discouraged.
>
> 3. **Board Courses & Clinical Programs**: Programs such as the **College of Nursing (CON)** and **College of Education (COE)** during teaching internships enforce strict professional grooming rules  -  including natural hair color (no loud/unnatural hair dye) and standard military/prescribed hair cuts for males.
>
> 4. Modest hair highlights are generally permitted in non-board programs as long as they adhere to general university decorum.

### K374 - Services Offered By Guidance

Source: [services/oss_student_services.json](<../../../rasa/actions/knowledge/services/oss_student_services.json>), pointer `/topics/13`.
Topic: `ask_guidance_services`. Intent: `ask_guidance_services`.

Answer checkpoint from the existing data:
> What are the services offered in the University Guidance Center?
>
> The services that the UGC offers the following services:
>
> Counseling Services: Counseling is considered as the core of guidance services. It aims to assist the students in their emotional, social, physical, spiritual, and cognitive needs. During this time of pandemic the University Guidance Center offers online counselling so that the guidance counselors can reach out to students easier and use the online platform to cater their personal issues, problems and concerns.
>
> Career and Job Placement Services: It is a support service of the University Guidance Center, it aims to address the pre-employment and employment needs of the graduating students and alumnae. The UGC schedules an annual Job Fair. Various agencies and company are invited to take part of the school's on-campus recruitment program. The UGC offers career seminars and orientation that cater the needs of the students.
>
> Testing Services: The student's individual strength and weaknesses in the area of personality, IQ and aptitude are assessed through the use of standardized tests. This is handled by the psychometricians. The center provides; Psychological testing for students and testing of faculty and staff applicants.
>
> Exit Interview: The graduating students are given an opportunity to discuss their future plans, career choices and various options for employment.

### K379 - Student Grievance & Anti-Bullying

Source: [services/oss_student_services.json](<../../../rasa/actions/knowledge/services/oss_student_services.json>), pointer `/topics/18`.
Topic: `student_grievance_and_complaints_process`. Intent: `student_grievance_and_complaints_process`.

Answer checkpoint from the existing data:
> If you experience bullying, harassment, or have grievances regarding academic concerns or faculty conduct, BukSU provides structured grievance channels:
>
> 1. For bullying, peer conflicts, or mental health distress: Visit the **Guidance and Counseling Center** in the Student Services Center for confidential support and mediation.
>
> 2. For formal complaints regarding a professor or academic matter: Submit an official written complaint to the **Department Chairperson** or the **College Dean**.
>
> 3. You may also consult the **Office of Student Services (OSS)** for student welfare and rights assistance under the BukSU Student Handbook.

### K384 - Dress Code Policy

Answer checkpoint from the existing data:
> **University Memorandum No. 01, s. 2026  -  Prescribed University Uniform Policy:**
> 
> Please be informed that all students are required to wear the complete prescribed university uniform every **Monday**, **Tuesday**, **Thursday**, and **Friday**, effective on their respective dates:
> 
> - **2ND YEAR - 4TH YEAR STUDENTS:** Effective **September 7, 2026**
> - **1ST YEAR STUDENTS:** Effective **September 14, 2026**
> 
> Students are expected to **strictly observe the prescribed university uniform policy** on the indicated days.
> 
> *(Note: **Wednesday** remains the official university **Wash Day** where casual/civilian attire is permitted. Wearing of shorts, sandos/sleeveless shirts, ripped clothes, and rubber slippers is strictly prohibited on campus during class days and office hours).*
>
> You can also read other BukSU Policies through this link: https://buksu.edu.ph/security-services-unit/

### K385 - BukSU General Policies

Source: [services/oss_student_services.json](<../../../rasa/actions/knowledge/services/oss_student_services.json>), pointer `/topics/24`.
Topic: `buksu_general_policies`. Intent: `buksu_general_policies`.

Answer checkpoint from the existing data:
> Here are some of the Bukidnon State University policies, you can also visit this BukSU official Website for more information about the policies of Bukidnon State University:
>  https://buksu.edu.ph/security-services-unit/
>
> **Dress Code and Personal Access**
> - Prohibited Attire: The security manual explicitly states: Proper and decent attire upon entering the BUKSU premises, offices shall be observed. Thus, **wearing of shorts and sando shall not be allowed to enter the school premises during class days and office hours** except during legitimate school activities with permission from the authorities.
> - "No ID, No Entry" Policy: All students across all levels and employees must wear or present their official school ID upon entering the campus.
>
> **Campus Curfew Policy**
> - College Students: Not allowed to stay inside the campus **beyond 9:30 PM** (unless attending official school evening activities).
> - General Campus Lockout: No **persons are allowed inside the campus beyond 10:00 PM** (including dorm residents, with exceptions for school officials and graduate students/DepEd Fellows logged by security).
>
> **Vehicle and Traffic Regulations**
> - Motorcycle Mufflers: Motorcycles with **modified mufflers that produce annoying or loud sounds are strictly banned** from entering the campus, even with a valid gate pass.
> - Minors / Students: A **No Driver's License, No Entry** policy is strictly enforced for elementary and high school student drivers from Monday to Sunday.
> - Vehicle Passes: Regular vehicles entering the campus must display a **valid Vehicle Gate Pass Sticker issued by the Office of the Chief Administrative Officer.** Visitors must leave a valid ID at the gate in exchange for a visitor's pass.

Answer checkpoint from the existing data:
> What are the office hours of Bukidnon State University?
>
> Bukidnon State University offices, including the Registrar's Office and the Accounting Office, operate only from Monday to Friday.
>
> Office hours are 8:00 AM to 12:00 NN and 1:00 PM to 5:00 PM.
>
> They are closed on Saturdays and Sundays.
>
> Make sure to plan your visits during the official office hours.
>
> For urgent matters, you can check if services are available online or contact the offices directly.
>
>  Contact Number: 0975 758 3157
>
>  Email: registrar@buksu.edu.ph
>
>  Facebook Page: https://www.facebook.com/BSURegistrar
>
>  BukSU Contact Number: 088-813-5661

>
> Food Technology Department: <b>Headed by Ms. Genessa Jesy T. Pagote.</b>
>
> Automotive Technology Department: <b>Headed by Dr. Rene M. Chavez.</b>
>
> Bachelor of Science in Entertainment and Multimedia Computing (BSEMC): <b>Program Chair Dr. Jovelin M. Lapates.</b>
>
> The administrative support for the college is handled by Mr. Raul D. Lecaros, the College Secretary.

### K442 - BukSU Seal Significance

Source: [university/university_identity.json](<../../../rasa/actions/knowledge/university/university_identity.json>), pointer `/topics/1/subtopics/3`.
Topic: `buksu_seal_significance`. Intent: `buksu_seal_significance`.

Answer checkpoint from the existing data:
> The BukSU Seal is the "sacred" and official emblem of Bukidnon State University, used primarily for high level academic and legal documents like diplomas and transcripts.
>
> Each element within the seal has a specific meaning:
>
> The Lamp: Symbolizes the light of truth and the university's commitment to academic, moral, and spiritual enlightenment.
>
> The Book: Represents knowledge and the historical record of the institution.
>
> The Adult and Child: Signifies the university's roots in teacher training, showing a teacher guiding a child toward a better future.
>
> The Mountains: Represents the university's location in Bukidnon and symbolizes the heights of wisdom.
>
> The Shield: Serves as the base for all symbols, representing education as a person's defense or shield against life's challenges.
>
> Laurel Leaves: Represents the excellence the university strives for in its graduates and faculty.
>
> Sheaf of Palay and Flask: These symbolize the university's goal of progress and prosperity for the region.

English:
- K442-EN-01: What does the meaning of the symbols in the BukSU seal mean at BukSU?
- K442-EN-02: Could you explain the meaning of the symbols in the BukSU seal in simple terms?

### K446 - Founding

Source: [university/university_identity.json](<../../../rasa/actions/knowledge/university/university_identity.json>), pointer `/topics/2/subtopics/1`.
Topic: `founding`. Intent: `founding`.

Answer checkpoint from the existing data:
> Bukidnon State University (BukSU) was founded in 1924 and celebrated its 101st Founding Anniversary on June 10, 2025. Over the years, the institution has undergone several important transformations in its development as a higher education institution in Malaybalay, Philippines.
>
> Its historical development can be traced through the following milestones:
>
> 1924  -  Established as Bukidnon Provincial High School (BPHS)
>
> 1928  -  Renamed Bukidnon Normal School (BNS), with a focus on teacher training
>
> 1972  -  Renamed Bukidnon Normal College (BNC)
>
> June 14, 1976  -  Converted into Bukidnon State College (BSC) through Presidential Decree No. 944
>
> May 15, 2007  -  Attained university status as Bukidnon State University under Republic Act No. 9456
>
> Today, BukSU is recognized as a public institution of higher learning known for its commitment to academic excellence, teacher education, and diverse academic programs.

> Bukidnon State University currently has a total of **16 campuses** (the **Main Campus** in Malaybalay City plus **15 Satellite Campuses**):
>
> - **Within Bukidnon Province (12 campuses)**: Baungon, Cabanglasan, Damulog, Impasug-ong, Kadingilan, Kalilangan, Kitaotao, Libona, Malitbog, Quezon, San Fernando, and Talakag campuses.
>
> - **In Misamis Oriental Province (3 campuses)**: Alubijid, Medina, and Talisayan campuses.
>
> For more details and program offerings across satellite campuses, visit: https://buksu.edu.ph/satellite_campus/
